english_verification.review_scope: Representative names, opening identity, source prose and actual fixed-revision Wiki passages, plus native national-idea text compared by localisation key. Large mission/idea ranges are locator envelopes, not exhaustive checks of every intervening line or runtime reachability.
unresolved: The source metadata use BOM-free LF-normalized text hashes. Raw CRLF byte hashes differ by design and do not establish stale content.

rationale.campaign_length: I04 has 36 direct missions, with long extensions through the production, cavalry, pasture, and hold branches.
rationale.colonization: The missions require restoring mountains, pastures, and plains and pushing into the northern passage.
rationale.complexity: Formation requirements, pastures, mining, branching armaments, and fiscal conditions interlock.
rationale.dark_story: The available evidence is mainly about war and resource control; systemic population harm is not confirmed.
rationale.difficulty: Resources, technology, disasters, and mission prerequisites must be managed together; not playtested.
rationale.diplomacy: Adventurer-company relations before formation and hold diplomacy afterwards matter, but are not the main loop.
rationale.early_pressure: The adventurer company, hold restoration, colonisation, and manpower limits create pressure before formation.
rationale.magic_artifice_intensity: Mechanical rams, forges, artificers, and prototype research directly reshape the unit route.
rationale.narrative_density: The lost hold, Ramsteel tradition, pastures, and mechanical cavalry form a continuous story.
rationale.tall_play: Holds, pastures, mines, and production buildings need sustained development.
rationale.trade_economy: Wool, livestock, iron, mithril, and forges connect production and trade.
rationale.warfare: Ramsteel cavalry, mechanical rams, and hold expansion define the late-game military arc.

identity.appearance: A Ramsteel Dwarf country formed by a Dwarven Adventurer company after meeting hold, administrative technology, peace, and city conditions.
identity.formation_scope: DiggyDwarvenFormables.txt defines I04_nation: the core of Hold 4147, a Dwarven administrative reform, administrative technology 7, peace, at least three cities, and the Dwarven mountain formation trigger; formation changes the culture to Ramsteel and replaces non-generic missions.

national_ideas.scope_note: National traditions, seven ideas, and ambition only; no optional idea groups or racial/government bonuses. Multiple sets and conditions are listed separately and are not simultaneous; whether formation accepts a new set depends on the actual event or decision and player choice.

description.text: The renowned chargers of dwarven ram cavalry in fact originated in Orlazam-az-dihr. The first ram rangers started life as frontier woodsmen and farmers who later formed a close bond with the native rams - it is said that a bond between an Ramsteel and their mount was stronger than that with their spouse!

description.text: During the days of Aul-Dwarov the Ramsteels were tasked with protecting the terraced farms of the Serpent's Vale against any would-be intruder from beyond, from early human tribes to trolls and ogres.

description.text: Before the age of Kronium, Adamantium and Mithril, there was Ramsteel. This steel was first forged by the ancient proto-dwarves who trained their rams to hit heated sheets of metal in order to harden it more than any ordinary dwarf could. Known for its hardness and durability, Ramsteel would go on to be the favoured metal for many warriors.

description.text: The greatest of the Ramlords of Orlazam was Tednur Fourfoot, who famously led a devastating cavalry charge against one of the largest goblin hordes in history. Records say the cavalry's wake was so devastating that the infantry following kept slipping and sliding on the mashed and slushed innards of goblins.

description.text: By the time Aul-Dwarov was founded the days of ramsteel dominance were long over and many dwarves focused and cultivated their mastery of meats and cattle. The Orlazam Lamb became a staple in the halls of dwarven kings, known for its juicy meats and sun-kissed flavours from the surface that were exotic to Orlazam's more underground-dwelling kin.

description.text: An infamous practice of the Ramlords against disobedient subjects was the Hornwall Punishment, which involved lining up the offending dwarves against the wall and having rams smash into them.

description.text: Loyalty to the High King was commonplace among the Ramsteel Dwarf Clans, as their cooperation with the neighbouring hold of Amldihr had brought prosperity for the nobles and ram herders. The two holds fostered very friendly relations with each other, often siding with each other in Amlharaz debates and other disputes. Land rights to the vale were granted for herds, many privileges for the hold and nobles were granted, and favouritism was practised due to Ramsteel loyalty. The Ram Riders fought to the end to aid the last High King against the orcs besieging in King’s Rock, even while having lost, they proved their loyalty to be unwavering.

player_overview.avoid_if: You want pure infantry, pure diplomacy, or no mountain development and Dwarven disaster management.
player_overview.how_it_plays: Form the hold country first, then use pastures and mining to fund progressively upgraded Ramsteel cavalry.
player_overview.overview: Orlazam-az-Dihr is a Ramsteel country formed after a Dwarven Adventurer company reclaims Hold 4147. Meet the hold, administrative technology, and city requirements, then develop pastures, irrigation, mines, and forges to upgrade ordinary Dwarven cavalry into mechanical rams. Before and after formation, colonisation, finances, production, and Dwarven disasters compete for attention.
player_overview.recommended_for: Players who enjoy unusual units, engineered economies, and steadily stacking military power.
signature_features: Ramsteel and ram husbandry make cavalry the central loop.
Pastures, iron, mithril, and forges lock into one another.
The mechanical-ram prototype requires technology, artificers, and major financial investment.
player_overview.tagline: Let dwarves ride mechanical rams and reforge the lost hold into a cavalry and industrial country.

reasons: Mechanical rams are a distinctive endgame that clearly changes combat.
Pastures, mining, and forges create a complete economic loop.
The hold-revival objective remains clear before and after formation.
warnings: The random mission script returns 0 for the formed-country file, whereas the structural database records 36 directly defined I04 missions; see the evidence page for the counting boundary.
The community posts are old-version experiences and their values are not adopted.

positive_indicators: Mining and forges serving public defence.
values.rationale: The missions invest in pastures, irrigation, cities, mines, and public defence, giving the country a strong public-good orientation; the available material provides limited evidence about population policy and treatment of residents. War, armaments, Dwarven identity, expansion, and state formation are not deductions by themselves, and no concrete systemic enslavement or population-as-resource harm is confirmed.
